text:
Jordan: heads up — noticing a handful of PRO-tier requests getting routed to eu-west instead of us-central. No 5xxs, just +~220ms latency and an unexpected model variant (v1 -> v1-quant).
Marta: @Jordan any correlation with a routing policy change? I scanned deploys, nothing obvious in the past hour.
Jordan: dug into route decision logs — request metadata shows preferred_region=us-central, fallback_chain=[us-central, eu-west]. Policy evaluation flagged eu-west due to capacity scoring, but us-central quotas looked fine.
Sahil: could be stale snapshots. Our scoring window is 30s — did we just change refresh behavior? @deploy-bot any recent deploys for routing-scorer?
deploy-bot: deploy 2026-11-02T12:03Z: routing-scorer v2 rolled to 30% canary
Ashley: that explains some canary noise. v2 changed slot-estimation erf and might underreport some us-central pools for GPU instance types.
Jordan: also worth noting: model variant mapping uses the compatible_variants table; v1-quant is marked compatible with v1 which allows fallback. For PRO tier we expect strict_variant_match=true, but the decision path seems to allow compatibility later in pipeline.
Kevin: why is variant compatibility assessed after region scoring? We have a policy that strict_variant_match applies for enterprise & pro customers. Is that flag being respected in the scorer?
Marta: checked SRE telemetry — the variant check was skipped when route decision took the fallback path because of a tie_breaker.
Sahil: tie_breaker sums latency_estimate + capacity_score. If capacity_score is stale it can nudge decision to second region before variant check runs.
Jordan: reproduce I used:
```\ncurl -X POST https://router/api/v1/evaluate -d '{"customer_tier":"pro","model":"redwood-1","region_hint":"us-central"}'
# response: chosen_region=eu-west, reason=capacity_score(0.72) > us-central(0.71)
```
Ashley: can you paste the scoring snapshot for 1800001000-1800001100?
Jordan: snippet:
```
us-central: capacity=0.71, last_refresh=1800000965
eu-west: capacity=0.72, last_refresh=1800001010
```
us-central refresh was 45s old.
Kevin: 45s > scoring_window(30s). Why didn't the scorer treat it as stale and force a sync refresh or mark as unavailable?
Marta: found the bug: stale_check was only applied to CPU-backed pools. routing-scorer v2 removed the implicit sync refresh fallback to avoid blocking decisions.
Sahil: OK root cause summary: routing-scorer v2 changed refresh behavior + canary exposure meant some requests used v2 path -> stale capacity snapshot + tie_breaker -> selects eu-west -> variant check happened later and got skipped in the fallback path -> silent redirects to other region and quant variant for PRO.
Jordan: impact numbers: ~0.15% of PRO requests experienced cross-region redirect + variant downgrade for ~10 minutes during the canary window.
Ashley: telemetry gap: we didn't log a routing-deviation event because our metrics only fire on 5xx or explicit region-mismatch flag. We should log when chosen_region != preferred_region regardless.
Kevin: immediate mitigations proposal:
- rollback routing-scorer v2 from canary
- enable strict_variant_check earlier in the pipeline (pre-scoring)
- add stale_as_unavailable setting for capacity snapshots
- emit routing-deviation and variant-mismatch metrics
- add a short circuit to prevent variant-downgrade decisions for PRO/enterprise
Marta: I can rollback v2 now. @deploy-bot trigger rollback.
deploy-bot: rollback initiated for routing-scorer v2 -> v1 (canary instances). ETA ~2m.
reliability-bot: incident created INC-2026-112: PRO-tier silent redirects -> assigned to eng-platform / SRE.
Jordan: action items:
- Marta: rollback (in progress)
- Sahil: add unit + integration tests for stale snapshot handling + verify stale_as_unavailable semantics
- Ashley: update telemetry: emit routing-deviation + variant-mismatch events and dashboards
- Kevin: update Console trace view to show region decision + variant selection per request
- Jordan: write postmortem with timeline and customer impact
Kevin: also recommend we change policy evaluation order: do tier & strict_variant checks before capacity tie-breaker to avoid routing away when policy forbids downgrade.
Sahil: small caveat — doing variant lookup earlier adds an extra metadata lookup in hot path. We'll cache compatibility table with TTL=5s and add a warmup to canary nodes.
Ashley: ping here when rollback is done and I'll validate telemetry queries.
deploy-bot: rollback complete at 1800001299.
Jordan: monitoring shows cross-region rate dropped back to 0.0% within ~20s after rollback.
Marta: we'll only reopen canary after fixes land and gate on metrics: routing-deviation < 0.01% and variant-downgrades = 0 for 24h.
Jordan: thanks all. I'll post a short summary in #postmortems and follow up with a draft action plan.
